title: From notebook to pipeline
outcome: Explain why a reproducible training/inference pipeline replaces a one-off notebook workflow, and identify the 5 stages a production ML pipeline must cover - ingestion, preprocessing, training, evaluation, inference.

title: Reading the provided pipeline scaffold
outcome: Trace how data moves through the provided training/inference pipeline scaffold from raw input to served prediction, and label each stage's purpose.

title: Adding and validating a bounded pipeline stage
outcome: Follow an expert adding one preprocessing or validation stage to the provided pipeline, then verify its input/output contract and confirm that the unchanged stages still run.

title: Explain-the-code checkpoint
outcome: Given an AI-generated addition to the pipeline, explain line by line what it does, test its input/output contract, and identify any part that needs correction before merging.

title: Batch vs real-time inference tradeoffs
outcome: Compare batch and real-time inference patterns - latency, cost, throughput - and justify which pattern the provided inference brief requires.

title: Pipeline extension deliverable
outcome: Deliverable: the provided pipeline scaffold extended with at least 1 validated stage, a line-by-line explanation of the changed logic, and a justified batch-vs-real-time recommendation for the inference brief.

title: Why ad hoc tracking breaks down at scale
outcome: Identify 3+ failure modes of tracking experiments manually (spreadsheets, notebook print statements) once a team runs many models, and explain why systematic tracking matters for auditability.

title: Controls, confounders, and decision metrics
outcome: Explain why a run comparison is invalid when dataset split, evaluation conditions, or multiple uncontrolled factors change, and distinguish a primary decision metric from diagnostic metrics.

title: Building the five-run experiment matrix
outcome: Define a five-run experiment matrix for the provided training and inference pipeline starter that holds the dataset split and evaluation conditions constant, names the factor varied in each comparison, selects a primary metric tied to the inference brief, and labels any run that is not directly comparable.

title: Revisiting MLflow in a pipeline context
outcome: Use the provided MLflow setup to log parameters, metrics, and artifacts automatically as part of the cumulative pipeline, building on basic experiment logging from T4 (AI track).

title: Comparing multiple runs systematically
outcome: Use the MLflow UI to compare 5+ experiment runs against each other and identify the best-performing configuration for a given metric.

title: Autologging and reducing manual tracking overhead
outcome: Configure autologging for the pipeline and explain the tradeoff between autologging convenience and control over what gets logged.

title: Validating an assistant-generated experiment summary
outcome: Direct an approved assistant to generate a summary comparison across logged experiment runs, validate every recommendation against the raw MLflow data and the declared primary metric, and flag any inaccuracy or invalid comparison.

title: Experiment tracking deliverable
outcome: Deliverable: at least 5 experiment configurations logged and compared in MLflow, an autologging setup, and an AI-assisted summary recommending which configuration to promote - with the summary validated against raw data.

title: From "which file is production?" to a registry
outcome: Explain 3 problems a model registry solves that ad hoc file-saving does not - versioning, alias/tag-based lifecycle control, and auditability - and recognise staging, production, and archived as superseded stage vocabulary replaced by aliases, tags, and environment-specific registered models.

title: Registering and promoting a model
outcome: Use the provided model registry scaffold to register a new model version, record its validation status with tags, and promote it by assigning the scaffold's active-model alias.

title: What full reproducibility requires
outcome: Identify the code version, data snapshot, parameters/configuration, environment, and model artifact that must be traceable together for a training run to be reproducible.

title: Reproducing a past training run
outcome: Given a past experiment logged in MLflow, use its recorded code, data, configuration, environment, and registry lineage to reproduce the evaluation result within the tolerance declared in the clean-state verification specification.

title: Rolling back a bad model version
outcome: Reassign the active-model alias from a bad version to the previous approved version, and document what the registry audit evidence captured during the rollback.

title: Registry lifecycle deliverable
outcome: Deliverable: a model registered, tagged with validation evidence, assigned the active-model alias, then rolled back by alias reassignment - with a documented audit trail and the lineage needed to reproduce the approved run within the tolerance declared in the clean-state verification specification.

title: Scoping the cumulative pipeline for production-grade reproducibility
outcome: Continue the pipeline built across Sprints 1-3 and scope the remaining work needed to meet the final criteria. A T4 (AI track) model may replace the baseline model only as a deliberate transfer test inside the same scaffold.

title: Integrating pipeline, tracking, and registry
outcome: Integrate the existing pipeline stages, MLflow tracking, registry aliases/tags, and inference-mode decision into one end-to-end run that trains, evaluates, logs, and registers a model version.

title: Proving the selected serving path uses the active version
outcome: Exercise the selected batch or real-time inference path with a representative input, verify that it resolves to the intended active model version, and capture the output plus the latency, throughput, or completion evidence named in the inference decision brief.

title: Setup, run, and expected-evidence instructions
outcome: Produce environment/setup and run instructions that start from the clean-state verification specification's declared clean state, name the data snapshot and exact execution command, and state the expected lineage fields, inference evidence, and result tolerance a second engineer must verify.

title: Proving the pipeline reproduces
outcome: Re-run the completed pipeline from the declared clean state, verify its lineage and result against the tolerance declared in the clean-state verification specification, and document and diagnose any divergence.

title: Reproducible pipeline deliverable
outcome: Deliverable: the cumulative end-to-end pipeline (train -> track -> register -> select active version -> exercise the selected inference path) reproduced from the declared clean state, with traceable code/data/configuration/environment lineage, reproducible setup/run instructions, inference evidence, and at least one non-trivial extension documented and explained.
